knowledge:
- key_parameters: <object=An object of class marrayRaw or marrayNorm containing the microarray data ;; X=Matrix of spot x-coordinates; if NA, spotted columns are used as proxies ;; Y=Matrix of spot y-coordinates; if NA, spotted rows are used as proxies ;; alpha=Vector of local regression smoothing parameters tested in GCV (default seq(0.05,1,0.1)) ;; iter=Number of iterations in the OLIN/OSLIN procedure (default 3) ;; OSLIN=Logical; if TRUE, performs subsequent optimized scaling of the range of M across the array ;; scale=Vector of scale parameters s tested in GCV to control multi-dimensional smoothing ;; weights=Matrix of prior spot weights; spots with zero or negative weights can be excluded from regression ;; genepix=Logical; if TRUE, adjusts GenePix-derived weights so that negative weights are excluded and non-negative weights are set to one ;; bg.corr=Background correction method for marrayRaw objects (e.g., "none", "sub", "movingmin", "minimum", "edwards", "normexp") ;; mode=Scaling method in bas ("var" for variance, "mad" for median absolute deviation, or "quantile")>
- alternatives: <Global linear normalization (fails to correct for non-linear dye bias) ;; Standard non-linear normalization methods like lowess/loess (rely on default parameters and require manual parameter tuning rather than automated GCV optimization) ;; OLINgui package (provides a graphical user interface for OLIN)>
- when_to_use: <When normalizing two-color cDNA microarray data affected by non-linear intensity-dependent and spatial (location-dependent) dye biases, provided that most genes are not differentially expressed (or up- and down-regulation is balanced) and genes are randomly spotted across the array.>
- pitfalls: <Violations of underlying assumptions (e.g., non-random spotting of genes or highly unbalanced differential expression) can lead to local regression over-adjusting the data and underestimating true differential expression ;; OSLIN is particularly sensitive to these violations, though sensitivity can be reduced by setting the minimum alpha parameter to larger values ;; OLIN/OSLIN is highly efficient and can make normalized data look clean and balanced regardless of the true underlying data quality ;; Local regression assumes smoothness of bias, meaning localized artifacts (scratches, bubbles, edge effects) must be flagged and masked using sig.mask prior to normalization to prevent them from distorting the fit>

workflows.name: within_array_normalization
workflows.intent: Perform optimized local intensity- and location-dependent normalization (OLIN/OSLIN) on a two-color microarray slide and visually inspect the results.
input: raw_microarray_data.RData (marrayRaw object containing spot intensities and layout)
spot_coordinates.RData (list or dataframe containing physical X and Y coordinates of the spots)
workflows.stages: 1. Load raw microarray data and spot coordinates ;; 2. Visually inspect raw foreground/background intensities and spatial/intensity-dependent dye biases ;; 3. Perform optimized local regression normalization (OLIN or OSLIN) ;; 4. Plot normalized data to verify the removal of systematic biases.
workflows.code:
data(sw)
fgbg.visu(sw[,3])
plot(maA(sw[,3]),maM(sw[,3]),xlab="A",ylab="M",pch='.')
mxy.plot(maM(sw)[,3],Ngc=maNgc(sw),Ngr=maNgr(sw),
                 Nsc=maNsc(sw),Nsr=maNsr(sw))
data(sw.xy)
mxy.abs.plot(maM(sw)[,3],Ngc=maNgc(sw),Ngr=maNgr(sw),Nsc=maNsc(sw),Nsr=maNsr(sw))
mxy2.plot(maM(sw)[,3],X=sw.xy$X[,3],sw.xy$Y[,3],
          Ngc=maNgc(sw),Ngr=maNgr(sw),Nsc=maNsc(sw),Nsr=maNsr(sw))
norm.olin <- olin(sw[,3],X=sw.xy$X[,3],Y=sw.xy$Y[,3])
plot(maA(norm.olin),maM(norm.olin),main="OLIN",pch=".")
mxy.plot(norm.olin,Ngc=maNgc(norm.olin),Ngr=maNgr(norm.olin),
                Nsc=maNsc(norm.olin),Nsr=maNsr(norm.olin),main="OLIN")
norm.oslin <- olin(sw[,3],X=sw.xy$X[,3],Y=sw.xy$Y[,3],alpha=c(0.1,1,0.1),OSLIN=TRUE)
plot(maA(norm.oslin),maM(norm.oslin),main="OSLIN",pch=".")
mxy.plot(norm.oslin,Ngc=maNgc(norm.oslin),Ngr=maNgr(norm.oslin),
                Nsc=maNsc(norm.oslin),Nsr=maNsr(norm.oslin),main="OSLIN")

workflows.name: between_array_scaling
workflows.intent: Scale the log ratios (M) across multiple normalized microarray slides in a batch to achieve a similar overall distribution.
input: normalized_microarray_data.RData (marrayNorm object containing within-array normalized data)
workflows.stages: 1. Load normalized microarray data ;; 2. Plot density distributions of log ratios for all arrays before scaling ;; 3. Perform between-array scaling using variance, MAD, or quantile methods ;; 4. Plot density distributions after scaling to confirm alignment.

workflows.name: statistical_bias_assessment
workflows.intent: Statistically assess and detect intensity-dependent, spatial, pin-dependent, and plate-dependent biases in microarray data using ANOVA and permutation tests.
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate neighborhood correlation on intensity and spatial scales ;; 2. Perform ANOVA to test for intensity-dependent bias ;; 3. Perform ANOVA to test for spatial block-wise bias ;; 4. Perform ANOVA to test for pin- and plate-dependent biases ;; 5. Run permutation tests to calculate False Discovery Rates (FDR) for intensity and spatial biases and plot the significant biased regions.
workflows.code:
A <- maA(sw[,3])
M <- maM(sw[,3])
Mav <- ma.vector(A,M,av="median",delta=50)
cor(Mav,M,use="pairwise.complete.obs")
MM <-  v2m(maM(sw)[,3],Ngc=maNgc(sw),Ngr=maNgr(sw),Nsc=maNsc(sw),Nsr=maNsr(sw),visu=FALSE)
MMav <- ma.matrix(MM,av="median",delta= 2,edgeNA=FALSE)
Mav <- m2v(MMav,Ngc=maNgc(sw),Ngr=maNgr(sw),Nsc=maNsc(sw),Nsr=maNsr(sw),visu=FALSE)
cor(Mav,M,use="pairwise.complete.obs")
print(anovaint(sw,index=3,N=10))
s <-  anovaspatial(sw,index=3,xN=8,yN=8,visu=TRUE)
print(anovapin(sw.olin,index=3))
print(anovaplate(sw.olin,index=3))
FDR <- fdr.int(maA(sw)[,3],maM(sw)[,3],delta=50,N=10,av="median")
sigint.plot(maA(sw)[,3],maM(sw)[,3],FDR$FDRp,FDR$FDRn,c(-5,-5))
M <- v2m(maM(sw)[,3],Ngc=maNgc(sw),Ngr=maNgr(sw),
                Nsc=maNsc(sw),Nsr=maNsr(sw),main="MXY plot of SW-array 1")
FDR <- fdr.spatial(M,delta=2,N=10,av="median",edgeNA=TRUE)
sigxy.plot(FDR$FDRp,FDR$FDRn,color.lim=c(-5,5),main="FDR")
